Croplands expands WEED-IT range with new releases, including orchard solution

 18-06 | Smart farming | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Combining SwarmFarm Robotics’ SwarmBot, WEED-IT optical spot spraying technology and the proven Pinto platform, the new implement enables growers to automate spraying operations while maximising accuracy and efficiency – delivering chemical savings and greater flexibility in chemistry application. Photo: Croplands

Australian company Croplands Equipment has unveiled a wave of new technology across its WEED-IT precision spraying range, headlined by the Series 2 Robot Ready Pinto and spanning a new large-scale broadacre platform, expanded retrofit capability and the company’s first optical spot spraying solution purpose-built for orchards.

Leading the new releases is the Series 2 Robot Ready Pinto, the next generation of Croplands’ autonomous spraying platform. Combining SwarmFarm Robotics’ SwarmBot, WEED-IT optical spot spraying technology and the proven Pinto platform, the new implement enables growers to automate spraying operations while maximising accuracy and efficiency – delivering chemical savings and greater flexibility in chemistry application.

The Series 2 brings targeted engineering refinements to the platform, including an upgraded tank design for improved centre of gravity, along with a suite of further enhancements developed for the demands of autonomous field operation.

Croplands WEED-IT Product Lead Lachlan Coom says the update reflects both grower feedback and the growing maturity of the autonomous spraying market. “The Series 2 Robot Ready Pinto builds on a platform that growers already trust, with dedicated design enhancements.”

New Pegasus platform 

Alongside the Series 2, Croplands is releasing a purpose-built WEED-IT-ready 36-metre truss boom mounted to its renowned Pegasus 7000L sprayer. The result is a more compact large-scale broadacre sprayer with twin tank and twin spray line capabilities, giving farmers a versatile machine capable of spot spraying, blanket spraying or both simultaneously.

The platform has been extensively field tested over the past two years ahead of its release. “We are excited about the launch”, says Coom. “It’s about delivering practical solutions that fit into real farming systems, while giving operators more flexibility in how and when they spray.”

Strong momentum is also building around Croplands’ WEED-IT Retrofit Kits, with the company’s engineering and field service teams having successfully installed optical spot spraying sensors across a wide range of sprayer brands. Self-propelled, linkage and trailed units from Case Patriot, John Deere, Goldacres, Fendt Rogator, Hayes and Hardi have all been retrofitted, reinforcing the adaptability of the WEED-IT system.

Coom: “We’ve worked on a broad mix of machines and so far, we haven’t come across a sprayer we couldn’t retrofit. Growers can upgrade existing equipment with WEED-IT technology and start seeing savings without needing to invest in a completely new unit.”

WEED-IT heading to the orchard

Those savings are driven by WEED-IT’s ability to significantly reduce chemical use, improve spraying efficiency and help combat herbicide resistance in hard-to-control weeds. The technology’s credentials are well established: over the past 15 years, Croplands has installed more than 25,000 WEED-IT sensors, primarily in broadacre applications where the system has redefined spraying practices and supported more sustainable farming outcomes.

Now, that same capability is being extended to horticulture with the introduction of the WEED-IT Orchard 4000 – the company’s first full-row optical spot spraying solution designed specifically for orchard weed control. The system delivers targeted herbicide application across entire rows, bringing the precision spraying benefits long available to broadacre growers to the tree crop market for the first time.

Supporting the full range is the WEED-IT DASH 10″ touchscreen, designed to give operators greater confidence and insight into their spraying performance, with remote upgrade and support capability built in. Croplands will have WEED-IT equipment and technology on display across several upcoming field days in Australia.

translationZh:
澳大利亚公司Croplands Equipment在其WEED-IT精准喷洒系列中推出了一系列新技术，其中主打产品是第二代机器人就绪型Pinto，此外还包括一款新型大型大田平台、扩展的改装能力，以及公司首款专为果园设计的光学定点喷洒解决方案。

**第二代机器人就绪型Pinto**

引领此次新品发布的是Series 2 Robot Ready Pinto，这是Croplands自主喷洒平台的下一代产品。该新机具结合了SwarmFarm Robotics的SwarmBot、WEED-IT光学定点喷洒技术以及久经考验的Pinto平台，使种植者能够实现喷洒作业自动化，同时最大化精度和效率——从而节省化学药剂，并在药剂施用方面获得更大的灵活性。

Series 2对该平台进行了针对性的工程改进，包括升级的罐体设计以改善重心，以及一系列为满足自主田间作业需求而开发的进一步增强功能。

Croplands的WEED-IT产品负责人Lachlan Coom表示，此次更新既反映了种植者的反馈，也体现了自主喷洒市场日益成熟。“Series 2 Robot Ready Pinto建立在种植者已经信赖的平台之上，并加入了专门的设计改进。”

**新型Pegasus平台**

与Series 2同时推出的，还有Croplands为其著名的Pegasus 7000L喷雾机配备的一款专为WEED-IT设计的36米桁架喷杆。其结果是形成了一款更紧凑的大型大田喷雾机，具备双罐和双喷雾管路能力，为农民提供了一台能够进行定点喷洒、全面喷洒或两者同时进行的多功能机器。

该平台在发布前已经过过去两年广泛的田间测试。“我们对此次发布感到兴奋，”Coom说。“关键在于提供能够融入实际农业系统的实用解决方案，同时让操作者在喷洒方式和时间上拥有更大的灵活性。”

**改装套件势头强劲**

围绕Croplands的WEED-IT改装套件，强劲势头也在积聚。该公司的工程和现场服务团队已成功在多种品牌的喷雾机上安装了光学定点喷洒传感器。来自Case Patriot、John Deere、Goldacres、Fendt Rogator、Hayes和Hardi的自走式、牵引式和悬挂式机型均已成功改装，这进一步印证了WEED-IT系统的适应性。

Coom表示：“我们已经在各种各样的机器上工作过，到目前为止，还没有遇到我们无法改装的喷雾机。种植者可以用WEED-IT技术升级现有设备，无需投资购买全新的设备就能开始节省成本。”

**WEED-IT进军果园**

这些节省得益于WEED-IT显著减少化学药剂用量、提高喷洒效率以及帮助对抗难防杂草抗药性的能力。该技术的实力早已得到验证：过去15年间，Croplands已安装超过25,000个WEED-IT传感器，主要应用于大田作物领域，该系统重新定义了喷洒实践，并支持了更可持续的农业成果。

如今，同样的能力正被扩展到园艺领域，推出了WEED-IT Orchard 4000——这是公司首款专为果园杂草防治设计的全行光学定点喷洒解决方案。该系统可对整行进行针对性除草剂施用，首次将大田种植者长期享有的精准喷洒优势带到了果树作物市场。

为整个系列提供支持的是WEED-IT DASH 10英寸触摸屏，旨在让操作者对其喷洒性能更有信心和洞察力，并内置了远程升级和支持功能。Croplands将在澳大利亚即将举行的多个田间日活动中展示WEED-IT设备和技术。
